solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Apple sent back this note

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a rennet is an old variety of dessert apple, also spelt reinette

explanation.surface: Someone returns an apple along with a banknote, as if paying for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The apple is the obscure rennet, not a Granny Smith or a computer company.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-pound banknote is called a tenner in everyday British speech.

clue.text: Run out crude oil here?

parts.note: a trip is a short run out, an outing

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters are in an unprocessed jumble

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a place has run out of unrefined petroleum.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the Libyan capital, in an oil-producing country.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, a country whose economy rests on its crude petroleum exports.

clue.text: Mealie nun after shift is deficient in this

definitions.text: Mealie nun after shift is deficient in this

indicators.note: a shift moves things around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pale, mealy-faced nun coming off a work shift lacks something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'mealie' as mealy, pale; such a pallid person lacks the dark skin pigment. A mealie is also South African maize.
explanation.definitionFit: Eumelanin is the dark brown-black pigment of skin and hair, so a pallid person has little of it.

clue.text: Drawing close new yard's fastener?

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
an earing is a small rope fastening a sail's corner to a ship's yard

explanation.surface: A sketch nearly done, with a new fastening for the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: The yard is a ship's spar, not a garden or a measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearing means approaching, coming closer, the same as drawing close.

clue.text: Attention-seeker's occasion for partner swapping?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the polite phrase said to catch someone's notice
second meaning: a dance in which one may cut in and take another's partner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Partner swapping' hints at something racier; it is a ballroom dance where you may cut in.
explanation.definitionFit: The polite interruption phrase also names a dance where anyone may take over someone else's partner.

clue.text: Without line dancing babe wants girl that grooves

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about into a new order
without means lacking, so one letter is left out

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A babe hoping for a girl who can really dance, without lining up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grooves' looks like dancing slang; here it is woodwork. The L of girl is the letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbeting saw cuts rabbets, the stepped recesses or grooves along a board's edge in joinery.

clue.text: Value support for single-decker, say

parts.note: to set a price on something is to value it
a tee supports a golf ball before it is struck

explanation.surface: Putting a price on the stand for a single-decker bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single-decker' suggests a bus; here it is a seat with one level, unlike a bunk bed, and 'say' flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a long upholstered seat with a single tier, as opposed to a double bunk.

clue.text: Home of leaders of coppers in disguise? Dastardly con possibly

definitions.text: Home of leaders of coppers in disguise?

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A villain's scam might hide where top police officers are based.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers in disguise' are plain-clothes detectives, headed from the Metropolitan Police headquarters in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Metropolitan Police headquarters, home of its senior officers and its detective branch.

clue.text: Core of poetic quip's heart is a case of pins and needles

definitions.text: a case of pins and needles

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central part, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the central pair of poetic

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the inner letters count

parts.note: the central pair of quip

explanation.surface: The essence of a witty poem is a tingling numbness.
explanation.walkthrough: Pins and needles sounds like a prickling sensation; it is literally the sewing kit inside a small case.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for holding sewing implements such as needles and pins.

clue.text: Peckham's man with a broom lacking general intelligence, good assiduous sport?

indicators.note: lacking means without, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: Trigger is the road sweeper in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses, set in Peckham, south London
g is the psychologists' symbol for general intelligence
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A dim but hardworking sitcom road sweeper is a good sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Trigger is famously slow-witted, which makes 'lacking general intelligence' apt in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A trier is someone who keeps making an effort, a persevering person who always tries hard.

clue.text: Number to call before getting something like a network?

parts.note: tel. is the abbreviation for a telephone number
a. abbreviates Latin ante, before

explanation.surface: Dialling a number before getting on a phone network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like an order instruction; it supplies a letter, as the abbreviation of ante.
explanation.definitionFit: A tela is a web-like tissue in anatomy, a membrane resembling a mesh.

clue.text: Bagel I sent back includes old pickle?

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters run backwards
what a phrase includes is contained within it, running across its words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of bagel, the I and the start of sent

explanation.surface: A bagel returned because it contains stale pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: Esile is an obsolete word for vinegar, the pickling liquid, used by Spenser and Shakespeare.

clue.text: She milks another who walked out on the boards?

definitions.text: She milks another who walked out on the boards?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, one who has left
the boards are the stage, and she is a woman performing there

explanation.surface: A woman exploits a rival who abandoned the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a woman who once milked applause on stage but has now walked out on it; 'She' keeps the performer female.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has given up stage performing is a former performer, hence the prefix ex- before the job title.

clue.text: One that gets muezzin going in the morning

definitions.text: One that gets muezzin going in the morning

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: getting something going means starting it, so only its opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of muezzin
a.m. marks times before noon

explanation.surface: A mosque leader prompting the caller to prayer at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of a mosque leader who sets the dawn call to prayer under way.
explanation.definitionFit: The imam leads prayers in a mosque, where the muezzin issues the call to prayer from the minaret.

clue.text: Stewed steak, say, at Le Manoir, yes with extravagant bill to cover

parts.note: surface padding: a French restaurant's name, signalling that the yes is French

indicators.note: to cover something is to go round it, so one piece wraps the other
extravagant suggests something wild and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
oui is French for yes

explanation.surface: A diner at Le Manoir, a grand French-style restaurant, gets a huge bill for stewed steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at Le Manoir' signals that the yes is French; Le Manoir aux Quat'Saisons is a famous Oxfordshire restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bouilli is French-style boiled or stewed meat, beef especially, so stewed steak is one example.

clue.text: Dutch person on the left is reckless

parts.note: per. is a dictionary abbreviation for person, as in grammar
Du. is the dictionary abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A Dutch politician on the left is accused of recklessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the left' tells you the person comes before the Dutch in the across answer, not a political wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdu has an old sense of desperate or foolhardy, from soldiers sent on hopeless missions, hence reckless.

clue.text: One of the Pieridae who gave the needle and ended it all

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a brimstone-like butterfly of the white and yellow family

definitions.text: who gave the needle and ended it all
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Egyptian queen whose name is on a London obelisk and who killed herself

explanation.walkthrough: 'gave the needle' sounds like annoying someone; it is the obelisk on the Thames Embankment named after her. 'Ended it all' is her suicide by asp.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is borne both by a yellow butterfly species and by the last Ptolemaic queen of Egypt.

clue.text: Old famous sort rejecting new vaudeville

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: rejecting something means throwing it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a lion is a celebrity, a famous person sought after socially
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A veteran celebrity turns down a new variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: A literary lion is a famous person; the dropped letter is the N at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An olio is a medley or miscellany, and specifically a variety entertainment of songs and sketches.

clue.text: Sovereignty sure fell in a chaotic state

indicators.note: things in chaos are jumbled out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A state's sovereignty certainly collapsed amid chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-rule is self-government, a nation's independent authority over itself.

clue.text: White friar's catechism beginning to illuminate

parts.note: Fra is the title of an Italian friar, here with its possessive
cat. is a dictionary abbreviation for catechism

indicators.note: a beginning is a start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of illuminate

explanation.surface: A white-robed friar's religious instruction starts to enlighten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' looks like the friar's habit; it is a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Frascati is a white wine from the hill town of that name near Rome.

clue.text: Gothic architectural features clash with a recent change

indicators.note: a change alters the arrangement, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gothic architecture jars with a recent alteration to a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancet arches are tall, narrow pointed arches typical of Early English Gothic churches.

clue.text: Tough PI struggling with nervous affliction

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hard-boiled private eye wrestles with his nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip gout is an old name for sciatica, pain from the sciatic nerve.

clue.text: We go under ignoring northerner's film — we give you little rest

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: snorkellers swim just below the surface
kell is a Scots and northern word for a caul, a thin membrane

explanation.surface: Underwater swimmers skip a northern movie and keep you awake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like cinema; it is a thin membrane in dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Snorers keep others awake with their noise, allowing their companions little sleep.

clue.text: Doubling the act of planting crops finally must be good

indicators.note: saying one thing must be another means it is swapped out and replaced

parts.note: insemination is sowing seed, literally or figuratively

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of a word, so only its closing letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of crops
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A farming instruction: planting crops properly at the end must be done well.
explanation.walkthrough: The S in the third position of the planting word is the last letter of crops, and it becomes a G.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingemination is repetition or reiteration, a twinning of words, from Latin geminus, a twin.

clue.text: Inappropriately tells to go old woman who's kept scraps

parts.note: miss is an old word for a kept mistress
ends are leftovers, as in odds and ends

explanation.surface: Someone rudely orders off an old lady who hoards scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old woman' looks like mother or missus; the archaic sense of kept mistress is what 'who's kept' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: To missend is to dispatch wrongly, so it means directing something or someone to go to the wrong place.

clue.text: Mould girl from The Broads entering capital initially

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: mor is East Anglian dialect for a girl; the Broads are Norfolk waterways
u.c. is the printers' abbreviation for upper case, capital letters

explanation.surface: Mould from a Norfolk girl first getting into the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city; it is a capital letter, abbreviated by its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucor is a genus of fungi that forms the common pin mould on bread and fruit.

clue.text: Soldier is to gather kit from the front

parts.note: shir, or shirr, is to gather fabric into rows of stitching

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of kit

explanation.surface: A soldier must collect his kit before going to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' looks like a noun; as a verb it means to dodge work, an old military slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier, in an old slang sense, is to malinger or avoid one's duties, as does a dodger.

clue.text: Colleague's operation into which one goes

parts.note: op is short for a surgical operation
a po is a chamber pot, which one goes into

explanation.surface: A workmate's surgery, which someone must undergo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into which one goes' sounds like going into theatre; it is the chamber pot, in toilet humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British slang for a mate or counterpart, especially a fellow serviceman, from 'opposite number'.

clue.text: God! More than 100 square metres

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Greek god of war
second meaning: the plural of a metric unit of land area equal to 100 square metres

explanation.walkthrough: 'God!' reads as an exclamation of surprise at the size; it is the war god of Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek war god shares his spelling with the plural of the land measure equal to a hundred square metres.

clue.text: Poet's Latin work picked up on those central to dupery

indicators.note: in a down answer, picking something up lifts it, so the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: op. abbreviates Latin opus, a work

indicators.note: the letters central to a word are those in its middle

parts.note: the central pair of dupery

explanation.surface: A poet's classical work taken up with deception at its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets one piece above the other in a down answer. The poet is Alexander Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope was an English poet of the eighteenth century, author of The Rape of the Lock.

clue.text: Westbound kid I see leaves having been wrapped up?

indicators.note: in an across answer, travelling west means right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease or kid them
taken as written
the letter C is said like see

explanation.surface: A boy heading west sees people going off after being bundled up warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb of departing; it is tobacco leaves rolled up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigar is a roll of tobacco leaves, an outer wrapper leaf binding the filler.

clue.text: Blighter bellows with joy about blue matter

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible fellow
io is a cry of triumph or joy in Greek drama
a. is a dictionary abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: A rogue roars happily over smutty material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bellows' looks like a verb; read it as a plural noun, shouts of joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Curiosa are erotic or pornographic books, the curious items in a collection; blue means indecent.

clue.text: Baron, or the equivalent, gets legal compo

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for baron
o.t.e. abbreviates 'or the equivalent', as in job advertisements

explanation.surface: A baron, or someone of similar rank, is awarded legal compensation.
explanation.walkthrough: Compo is British slang for compensation; the answer is an old legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: In old English law, bote was a payment or recompense made for injury or damage.

clue.text: Recurrent bind over admitting revision gives too testing rôles

indicators.note: admitting something lets it inside, so one piece goes within the others
recurrent here means running back again, so the letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: to strap is to bind
rev. is an abbreviation for revision
o is a cricket scoring abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A recurring legal bind-over admits a revised order, making roles too demanding.
explanation.walkthrough: Bind and over look like the legal phrase 'bind over'; they are separate pieces. Over's own letters then reappear in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To overpart an actor is to cast them in a role beyond their abilities.

clue.text: Again awry in the matter of coping? No longer free from risk

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
skew means askew, awry

explanation.surface: A wall built crooked again, as regards its top stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the matter of coping' is a second route to the same letters, re (about) plus skew (a coping stone). 'No longer' marks an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reskew is an obsolete spelling of rescue, to deliver from danger.

clue.text: First of demotic Greek characters for vessels

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of demotic
iota is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Demotic, the everyday modern Greek language, comes first in a passage about Greek letters used for vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A diota is an ancient two-handled jar, so the plural names those vessels.
